ESAB introduces ROBBI AI for adaptive cobot welding

The system generates weld paths and adapts to joints within procedure limits, using local computing at the factory.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Generating paths instead of teaching every point

ESAB detailed ROBBI AI for MIG and TIG on October 22. Operators position it near a joint and supply materials, consumables, weld type and WPS parameters. Sensing identifies the joint and generates a path, targeting low-volume, high-mix work and variable fit-up.

Adaptation inside procedure limits

ESAB says AI can adjust travel, oscillation and welding parameters as gaps change, or stop on conditions that threaten quality. InduSuite helps constrain decisions to specified procedures and qualification requirements. Operators can also disable full-AI mode for conventional cobot use.

Local data and application validation

Simulation precedes deployment, while weld data and video collected onsite support defect review. Computing stays at the facility without requiring continuous cloud communication. Claimed capabilities still need validation against customer materials and WPS; the announcement does not replace application-specific quality inspection.
